problem: Audio-visual navigation (AVN) policies fuse audio and visual features by late concatenation at the policy level, with no explicit alignment between sound and the visual regions of the source. They memorize 'acoustic fingerprint-scenario' correlations and fail on unheard sounds and unseen scenes.
motivation: Open-world agents cannot be trained on every sound, so generalization to unheard sources matters. SOTA methods exceed 95% SR on heard sounds but drop to about 50% on unheard ones. Humans turn toward a sound, focus on the likely region, then confirm with vision, so audio should decide where to look.
key_idea: Use audio self-attention context as the Query in cross-modal guided attention over visual features, so sound reweights sound-related visual regions before the GRU/PPO policy ('sound first, vision follows').
insight: Removing guided attention (w/o GA) causes big drops, e.g. Replica Depth SPL 80.2 to 43.1 and SNA 51.3 to 22.4, so feature-level audio-to-vision guidance is the key. Removing self-attention (w/o SA) also hurts, e.g. Matterport3D Depth SPL 63.3 to 46.6. Gains are largest on unheard sounds, which suggests spatial guidance reduces reliance on acoustic fingerprints. However, no controlled test of the fingerprint-memorization claim is given.
method: Encoders: Depth or RGB visual encoder and a binaural-spectrogram audio encoder produce audio features A (B×T×d) and visual features V (B×N×d).
Self-Attention (SA): multi-head self-attention applied separately to audio (global temporal context, A_SA) and to visual regions (region-to-region context).

Guided-Attention (GA): Transformer-style cross-attention with audio context A_SA as the Query and visual features as Key/Value, followed by residual+LayerNorm and an FFN, yielding audio-guided visual features V_GA (the equations as printed have Q/K/V roles inconsistent with this description).
Temporal modeling: the aligned multimodal representation is fed to a GRU across time steps.
Policy: PPO-based actor-critic head outputs action distribution and value from the GRU state; trained end-to-end following the SoundSpaces protocol.

setting.backbone: SoundSpaces-style encoders + SA/GA Transformer modules + GRU + PPO actor-critic (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces audio-visual navigation on Replica and Matterport3D; heard = telephone ring only; unheard = 102 sounds split 73/11/18 train/val/test; no extra data
setting.observation: Depth or RGB egocentric image + binaural spectrogram
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (SoundSpaces default), no waypoints

numbers.eval_set_note: Replica, Unheard sound, Depth, unseen scenes
Matterport3D, Unheard sound, Depth, unseen scenes

numbers_note: Split names are not stated explicitly in the paper; 'test' is assumed (unheard evaluation is on unseen scenes). RGB heard results (Replica 70.3/78.2/37.8; MP3D 49.8/83.5/17.7) are in Table 2 but not listed as separate entries.
results: On unheard sounds under Depth, AGVP reaches Replica SR 66.5 / SPL 46.8, beating AV-WaN (52.8 / 34.7), and Matterport3D SR 60.8 vs AV-WaN 56.7. Under RGB it clearly beats the SoundSpaces baseline (Replica unheard SR 63.8 vs 35.6). AV-WaN still has higher SNA on Matterport3D unheard (30.6 vs 19.1) and higher SPL and SNA on heard sounds.
limitations: Weaker on Matterport3D and on SNA, and on heard-sound SPL/SNA versus AV-WaN; the authors also say larger datasets remain challenging.
Only static single sound sources; no moving or multi-source evaluation, and no comparison with FSAAVN or other recent AVN methods; RGB compared only to the SoundSpaces baseline.
The spurious acoustic-fingerprint claim is not directly tested; the ablations are minimal, with no seeds or variance.
